purpose: Gives the investigation and follow-up pathway for a solid pulmonary nodule on CT in adults, whether detected incidentally in routine practice, on surveillance after previous malignancy, or by lung cancer screening.
system: British Thoracic Society guidelines for the investigation and management of pulmonary nodules: solid-nodule pathway

inputs.label: Clear benign features
inputs.how_stated: true when the nodule has a benign calcification pattern (diffuse, central, laminated or popcorn), macroscopic fat (e.g. hamartoma), or is a typical perifissural or subpleural nodule (smooth, solid, lentiform or triangular, within 1 cm of a fissure or pleura, under 10 mm); false when none of these is described

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: initial assessment of the probability of malignancy

inputs.label: Nodule type
inputs.how_stated: solid; part-solid (solid and ground-glass components); or nonsolid (pure ground-glass). For multiple nodules, the largest one.

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b: nodule type

inputs.label: Maximum diameter
inputs.how_stated: maximum diameter of the nodule in millimetres, e.g. '9 mm nodule'; for multiple nodules, the largest

inputs.label: Age
inputs.how_stated: patient age in years, usually from the request details

inputs.label: Nodule already proven to be lung cancer or a metastasis
inputs.how_stated: true only when this nodule has been shown on histology or cytology (biopsy or resection) to be lung cancer or a metastasis from another cancer, e.g. 'biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma'; false when this nodule is described as new, indeterminate or not yet sampled. A known cancer elsewhere, or a nodule merely suspected to be malignant, does not make it true.

locator.section: Groups not covered: B. Adults where the nodule in question has been pathologically shown to represent lung cancer or a pulmonary metastasis from another cancer

inputs.label: Sex
inputs.how_stated: patient sex, usually from the request details

inputs.label: Family history of lung cancer
inputs.how_stated: true when a first-degree or other family history of lung cancer is given in the clinical details

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b: family history of lung cancer

inputs.label: Emphysema on CT
inputs.how_stated: true when any emphysema is reported on this CT; false when the lungs are described without emphysema

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b: emphysema

inputs.label: Upper lobe location
inputs.how_stated: true for a right or left upper lobe nodule; false for middle or lower lobe (whether the lingula counts as upper lobe is not stated by the source: treat as left upper lobe)

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b: nodule location

inputs.label: Number of nodules
inputs.how_stated: total number of nodules on this CT, e.g. 'solitary' is 1, 'three nodules' is 3

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b: nodule count

inputs.label: Spiculation
inputs.how_stated: true when the nodule margin is described as spiculated; false for smooth, well-defined or lobulated margins

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b: spiculation

inputs.label: Prior CT showing the nodule
inputs.how_stated: true only when this nodule itself is described on an earlier study, e.g. 'unchanged since 2023', 'previously 6 mm', 'stable compared with the prior CT'; false when this is the first study to show it, e.g. 'new since the prior study', 'no previous imaging'. A whole-study fact: such a statement anywhere in the request or the report counts. A comparison line that does not mention this nodule (e.g. 'Comparison: CT 2023') settles neither: leave it out

inputs.label: Nodule resolved
inputs.how_stated: true when a nodule seen on an earlier CT is no longer visible on this CT; false whenever the nodule is seen and described on this CT

inputs.label: Growth assessment against the baseline CT
inputs.how_stated: volumetry when nodule volumes (mm3) from volumetry software are compared with the baseline CT; otherwise growth judged on diameter (2D) measurement or comparison: diameter_stable when unchanged in diameter, diameter_clear_growth when clearly larger, diameter_indeterminate for any other change such as a small or equivocal increase or a decrease (BTS gives no 2D growth threshold)

inputs.label: Baseline volume
inputs.how_stated: nodule volume on the baseline (first) CT in cubic millimetres, from volumetry software; always above 0

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: imaging follow-up

inputs.label: Current volume
inputs.how_stated: nodule volume on this CT in cubic millimetres, measured with the same volumetry software; always above 0 (for a nodule no longer visible, use the resolved input instead)

inputs.label: Interval from baseline CT
inputs.how_stated: days between the baseline CT and this CT, above 0, e.g. 3 months is about 91 days, 1 year is 365 days

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule with clear benign features (benign calcification, macroscopic fat, or typical perifissural or subpleural nodule).
outcomes.recommendation: No follow-up or further investigation needed.
caveats: Larger intrapulmonary lymph nodes may be followed up, especially with a known extrapulmonary primary cancer.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: initial assessment of the probability of malignancy

outcomes.classification: Sub-solid nodule (part-solid or pure ground-glass): outside the BTS solid-nodule pathway.
outcomes.recommendation: Manage with the BTS sub-solid nodule algorithm, starting with repeat thin-section CT at 3 months.
caveats: Sub-solid nodules under 5 mm need no follow-up.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: management of sub-solid nodules (SSNs)

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band} in maximum diameter.
outcomes.recommendation: No nodule follow-up needed.
caveats: With previous or active cancer, follow-up of nodules this small is a matter of clinical judgement (BTS correction, December 2015).
Equivalent volumetric threshold is under 80 mm3.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, no prior imaging for comparison.
outcomes.recommendation: CT surveillance: repeat CT 1 year after baseline and assess growth by volume doubling time.
caveats: Unfit for any treatment: BTS advises discharge instead.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, no prior imaging for comparison.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, Brock malignancy risk {brock_band}.
outcomes.recommendation: CT surveillance: repeat CT at 3 months and 1 year after baseline, assessing growth by volume doubling time.
caveats: Consider PET-CT for larger nodules in younger patients: the Brock model was developed in a 50-75-year-old screening cohort.
Unfit for any treatment: BTS advises discharge instead.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, Brock malignancy risk {brock_band}.
outcomes.recommendation: PET-CT if the nodule is above the local PET-CT detection threshold, then reassess risk with the Herder model.
caveats: Management after the Herder risk assessment is outside this entry.
Unfit for any treatment: BTS advises discharge instead.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule with significant growth (25% or more by volume), volume doubling time {vdt_band}.
outcomes.recommendation: Further investigation (biopsy, imaging or resection) and consideration of definitive management.
caveats: With a known extrapulmonary primary cancer, interpret growth in the context of the primary and its treatment.

outcomes.recommendation: Consider biopsy or ongoing yearly CT surveillance, guided by patient preference.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule growing slowly at 1 year or more from baseline: volume doubling time {vdt_band}.
outcomes.recommendation: Consider discharge or ongoing CT surveillance, taking account of patient preference, fitness and age.
caveats: Discharge is an option only when growth was assessed by volumetry.
With a known extrapulmonary primary cancer, interpret growth in the context of the primary and its treatment.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, stable on volumetry (volume change under 25%) at 1 year or more from baseline.
outcomes.recommendation: Discharge from nodule follow-up.
caveats: Applies to volumetric growth assessment; if growth is judged on 2D diameters, BTS advises CT follow-up for a total of 2 years.
With a known extrapulmonary primary cancer, interpret growth in the context of the primary and its treatment.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, smaller than at baseline at 1 year or more (negative volume doubling time).
outcomes.recommendation: No growth at 1 year: discharge as for a stable nodule.
caveats: BTS gives no separate step for a shrinking nodule; its evidence review reports a low cancer probability for shrunken or resolved nodules.
Applies to volumetric growth assessment; if growth is judged on 2D diameters, BTS advises CT follow-up for a total of 2 years.
With a known extrapulmonary primary cancer, interpret growth in the context of the primary and its treatment.

outcomes.classification: Previously seen nodule has resolved on this CT.
outcomes.recommendation: No further nodule follow-up.
caveats: Library addition, not BTS text: BTS gives no step for a resolved nodule; its evidence review reports a low probability of cancer for resolved or shrunken nodules.

outcomes.recommendation: Further investigation (biopsy, imaging or resection) and consideration of definitive management.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, stable on 2D diameter measurement at 1 year or more from baseline.
outcomes.recommendation: Repeat CT 2 years after baseline, then assess volume doubling time; discharge if stable.
caveats: Growth judged on 2D diameters needs CT follow-up for a total of 2 years (BTS).

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}, stable on 2D diameter measurement at 2 years or more from baseline.
outcomes.recommendation: Discharge from nodule follow-up.
caveats: BTS asks for a volume doubling time assessment at the 2-year CT; discharge applies when the nodule is stable.

outcomes.classification: Solid nodule {diameter_band}: diameter change since baseline not clearly growth or stability.
outcomes.recommendation: Assess growth by volumetry (volume doubling time) where available.
caveats: Library routing, not a BTS step: BTS defines significant growth by volume (25% or more) and gives no diameter growth threshold.

outcomes.recommendation: Manage per the clinical context.

summary.text: BTS 2015 pathway for solid pulmonary nodules in adults: discharge benign-looking and very small nodules, follow up small nodules with CT, and risk-assess larger nodules with the Brock model.

locator.table: Figure 1 Initial approach to solid pulmonary nodules

summary.text: Nodules 8 mm or more without prior imaging are scored with the Brock model; 10% or more leads to PET-CT and Herder reassessment, under 10% to CT surveillance.

locator.table: Figure 1 Initial approach to solid pulmonary nodules

summary.text: Growth is judged by volumetry and volume doubling time at 3 months and 1 year; 25% or more volume change counts as significant growth.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: imaging follow-up

summary.text: VDT 400 days or less prompts work-up; 400-600 days, biopsy or yearly surveillance; over 600 days, discharge or surveillance; stable at 1 year, discharge.

locator.table: Figure 2 Solid pulmonary nodule surveillance algorithm

definitions.text: Volume doubling time (VDT): days for the nodule volume to double, from two volumes and the interval: ln 2 x interval / ln(current / baseline volume). Negative when the nodule shrinks.

locator.section: Appendix 1: VDT calculation

definitions.text: Significant growth: a volume increase of 25% or more. Stability: volume change under 25% on CT after 1 year.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: imaging follow-up

definitions.text: Brock (PanCan) model: logistic model of cancer probability from age, sex, family history, emphysema, nodule size, type, upper-lobe location, nodule count and spiculation (full model with spiculation).

locator.table: Table 2, model 2b

definitions.text: Clear benign features: diffuse, central, laminated or popcorn calcification; macroscopic fat; typical perifissural or subpleural nodule (smooth, solid, lentiform or triangular, within 1 cm of a fissure or pleura, under 10 mm).

definitions.text: Pulmonary nodule: focal rounded opacity up to 3 cm, mostly surrounded by aerated lung, without related thoracic abnormalities such as lymphadenopathy.

pitfalls.text: BTS also gives volumetric size thresholds (80 mm3 and 300 mm3); this entry uses maximum diameter only for the size steps.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations

pitfalls.text: Does not apply to children under 18, or to nodules already proven to be lung cancer or metastasis. Opacities over 3 cm are masses, not nodules.

locator.section: Groups not covered

pitfalls.text: Previous or active cancer: follow-up below the 5 mm discharge threshold is a matter of clinical judgement (BTS correction, December 2015).
Brock was developed in current or former smokers aged 50-75. BTS recommends it for nodules 8 mm or more in smokers aged 50 or over, and suggests it for all patients.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: initial assessment

pitfalls.text: With multiple nodules, base the risk assessment on the largest nodule; nodule count still enters the Brock model.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations

pitfalls.text: Measure VDT from the baseline CT; volumes differ between software packages, so use the same one. Growth judged on 2D diameters needs 2 years of follow-up.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations: imaging follow-up

pitfalls.text: Patients unfit for any treatment are discharged at the first step of the BTS algorithm; this entry does not ask about fitness.

pitfalls.text: Herder risk after PET-CT and the sub-solid nodule algorithm are not encoded here.

pitfalls.text: Growth judged on diameters only (no volumetry): stable at 1 year goes to CT 2 years after baseline, then discharge if stable; clear growth goes to work-up. BTS sets no 2D growth threshold, so other changes are routed to volumetry.
